sources.title: Hydraulic Condition Monitoring — reproducible ML case study
sources.potentialUse: Reproducible offline evaluation reference; validate its split strategy and dataset terms before use.
sources.reportedScope: UCI hydraulic condition monitoring dataset; notebook, exported model, FastAPI demo.
sources.licenseStatus: repository code MIT; UCI dataset terms are separate
sources.accessStatus: README and LICENSE reviewed
sources.codeLicense: MIT (LICENSE file; GitHub API metadata reports NOASSERTION).
sources.dataLicense: Underlying UCI dataset 447 is CC BY 4.0; the exported joblib model and derived artifacts have no separate rights statement in the reviewed files.
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the notebook's grouped/stratified operating-block split, the leakage ablation, the model metadata and reported metrics. Raw UCI data were not downloaded and the joblib model was not executed.
sources.dataOrigin: UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 447 (ZeMA hydraulic test rig); the project targets valve-condition classification.
qualityNotes: The model classifies valve condition levels; it does not identify root causes or provide repair procedures.

The notebook uses StratifiedGroupKFold by operating-condition block. Its reported Random Forest ablation falls from CV-F1 0.977 on a random cycle split to 0.527 on a blockwise split, demonstrating severe leakage risk.
The final reported model is Gradient Boosting with test accuracy 0.906 and macro-F1 0.873; Brier 0.152 and ECE 0.023 are reported by the repository and were not independently reproduced.
The dataset is a laboratory test rig with class imbalance and no field validation; the model artifact's redistribution terms are not separately declared.
sources.dataLeakage: Preserve the StratifiedGroupKFold/operating-block separation. Never randomly split adjacent or near-identical cycles. External validation by physical rig/site is still absent.
sources.dependencies: Python scientific stack including NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, optional imbalanced-learn, FastAPI and joblib; not an Android/Worker dependency.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Offline evaluation reference only; do not ship the Python stack or pre-trained model in the PWA/Worker.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT applies to repository code. UCI data retain CC BY 4.0 attribution. Do not copy the model artifact or derived outputs until their separate redistribution rights are clear.

qualityNotes: The project explicitly predicts current component condition/severity, not time-to-failure or RUL.
Pump target is the UCI pump_leakage label; it is not a causal pump fault diagnosis or a repair procedure.
Reported GroupKFold metrics are laboratory/test-rig results and are not field validation.
The README explicitly states that real-system extrapolation is future work and not validated.
sources.dataLeakage: The notebook groups by operating point so cycles from one of the 144 design cells do not cross train/test folds. Still requires external validation on independent equipment/sites before operational use.
sources.dependencies: Python with NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn and Jupyter; no Android/Worker runtime.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Use methodology only; do not ship Parquet, PDFs or Python models in the PWA/Worker.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT applies to code. UCI data require CC BY 4.0 attribution. Do not redistribute processed Parquet or model artifacts until their separate rights are explicit.

sources.title: Brick Schema — building equipment and point ontology
sources.potentialUse: Reference for HVAC equipment classes, point types, system topology and equipment relationships; map only a small reviewed subset to the Toolkit's equipment/measurement schema.
sources.reportedScope: RDF/OWL class hierarchy and relationships for building subsystems, equipment and points; includes chiller-plant example.
sources.licenseStatus: BSD-3-Clause LICENSE inspected; ontology metadata points to repository LICENSE.
sources.accessStatus: README.md, LICENSE, bricksrc/ontology.py and examples/chiller-system/chiller-plant.ttl reviewed; no runtime parser was installed or executed.
sources.dataLicense: BSD-3-Clause for the reviewed repository ontology/example files; no third-party dataset payload reviewed.
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the RDF/OWL building metadata model, license metadata and a chiller-plant example linking chillers, chilled-water pumps, cooling towers, sensors and points with units.
sources.dataOrigin: Brick Consortium ontology and repository-authored example model; the example is illustrative metadata, not measured plant telemetry.
qualityNotes: Strong equipment/point topology vocabulary for HVAC; not a fault taxonomy, diagnosis model or repair procedure.
The chiller example describes topology and point semantics, not measured values or validated failure behaviour.
RDF/OWL and SHACL are heavier than the current browser runtime; a constrained JSON mapping is preferable.
sources.dataLeakage: Not a diagnostic dataset; no model evaluation. If later paired with telemetry, split by building/site and equipment rather than random time windows.
sources.dependencies: RDF/OWL/SHACL tooling and Python RDFLib for repository tooling; no dependency should be added to the Android PWA or Worker.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Use only a small static JSON subset of classes, relationships and point semantics; no full RDF reasoner in runtime.
sources.reuseConditions: Retain BSD-3-Clause notices and attribution; verify any imported external ontology namespaces and dependencies separately.
